I’ve just tried to get the specific algorithmic details from the STM paper via the WebFetch tool, but the response only gave a high‑level summary and explicitly said that the document lacks concrete specifications (thresholds, floor values, epoch counts, etc.). Since the user explicitly asked for “everything available” from the paper—including any verbatim code snippets, thresholds, pseudocode, and other technical details—I need to retrieve the full raw text of the paper myself rather than rely on the summarized excerpt.

The WebFetch call gave me the URL:
`https://glint-research-glint-research-papers.static.hf.space/Papers/STM_paper-md.html`
I can directly download that page with `curl`. However, the page is HTML‑formatted, and I need the plain text content (the Markdown source rendered as HTML). To extract the readable text, I’ll pipe the HTML through a small Python one‑liner that:

1. Reads the entire stdin.
2. Strips out any `<script>` and `<style>` blocks (they’re irrelevant and may contain JavaScript or CSS that would clutter the output).
3. Removes all remaining HTML tags via a regex `<[^>]+>`.
4. Unescapes HTML entities (e.g., `&` → `&`) using `html.unescape`.
5. Prints the cleaned text to stdout.

I’ll redirect that cleaned output to a temporary file (`/tmp/stm_paper.txt`) so I can inspect it later and also to know how large it is. A quick line count (`wc -l`) will give me a sense of the file’s length and confirm that the download succeeded.

All of this can be done in a single Bash command, which is exactly what the Bash tool expects: a command string and a brief description. The description should make clear that the purpose is to “Download and strip STM paper HTML” so the tool logs the intent correctly.

Thus, the appropriate next step is to invoke the Bash tool with the composed command:

```
curl -s "https://glint-research-glint-research-papers.static.hf.space/Papers/STM_paper-md.html" \
| python3 -c "import sys,html,re; t=sys.stdin.read(); t=re.sub(r'<script.*?</script>','',t,flags=re.S); t=re.sub(r'<style.*?</style>','',t,flags=re.S); t=re.sub(r'<[^>]+>','',t); print(html.unescape(t))" \
> /tmp/stm_paper.txt; wc -l /tmp/stm_paper.txt
```

This will fetch the full paper, clean it, store it, and report its line count, giving me the raw material needed to extract the exact algorithmic details the user wants.
